scenarios.title: Tornado Warning at Home
scenarios.description: A tornado warning has just been issued for your area. You're at home and need to take shelter immediately.

choices.text: Go to a small interior room with no windows on the lowest floor
choices.feedback: Correct. A small windowless room like a bathroom or closet on the lowest floor offers the best protection from flying debris and high winds.

choices.text: Watch the storm from a window to see how close it is
choices.feedback: Flying debris causes most tornado injuries and deaths, and windows can shatter violently. Always move away from windows during a tornado warning.

choices.text: Go to the largest room in the house, like the living room
choices.feedback: Large rooms often have wide roof spans that are more likely to collapse. Small, windowless rooms with sturdy walls hold up far better.

scenarios.title: Caught Outdoors
scenarios.description: You're outside on a walking trail when you spot a tornado forming in the distance, and there's no sturdy building nearby.

choices.text: Lie flat in a low ditch or depression and cover your head
choices.feedback: Correct. When no sturdy shelter is available, getting as low as possible and covering your head and neck reduces the risk of injury from debris and wind.

choices.text: Run toward the nearest large tree for cover
choices.feedback: Trees can be uprooted or have branches torn off in high winds, making them dangerous, not protective. Stay away from trees during a tornado.

choices.text: Try to outrun the tornado on foot
choices.feedback: Tornadoes can move unpredictably and far faster than a person can run. Seeking low ground nearby is safer than trying to outrun it.

scenarios.title: Driving When a Tornado Appears
scenarios.description: You're driving and spot a tornado in the distance, moving toward the road ahead. There's an overpass just up the highway.

choices.text: Pull over away from traffic, stay in the car with your seatbelt on, and duck below the windows
choices.feedback: Correct. If you can't safely drive away from the tornado's path, staying belted in your car with your head below window level is safer than exposed alternatives.

choices.text: Drive to the overpass and shelter underneath it
choices.feedback: Overpasses can create dangerous wind tunnels and offer little real protection from flying debris. This is a common myth. Avoid sheltering under them.

choices.text: Speed up to try to drive past the tornado's path
choices.feedback: Tornado paths are unpredictable, and vehicles are especially vulnerable to high winds. Racing toward or alongside it is extremely risky.
